item.title: Prices cut and production drops as Chinese cars flood UK market
item.description: Established car manufacturers are being forced to discount heavily in the face of cheap competition from China, the head of the UK's industry lobby group has admitted.
item.media:description: Employees work on the production line at a factory of Chinese electric vehicle (EV) maker Nio in Hefei, Anhui province, China April 2, 2025. REUTERS/Florence Lo

item.title: Czech FA president backs Infantino's $20bn World Cup sale plan
item.description: The president of the Czech Republic's football association has welcomed FIFA's bombshell plan to sell stakes in the World Cup's commercial rights - an endorsement which could complicate any move by the European body UEFA to boycott future global events.

item.title: 'Scandal within a scandal': Anger over delay to govt review of its Post Office convictions
item.description: The widow of a sub-postmaster says she is "extremely" frustrated as a review into the handling of prosecutions of Post Office staff is yet to begin nearly a year after being announced.

item.title: Manchester City propose change to New Deal transfer levy proposal
item.description: Manchester City are among a small number of top-flight clubs seeking alternatives to a 50% hike in the domestic transfer levy to help fund a landmark £1.5bn deal with the English Football League (EFL).
item.media:description: Man City v Chelsea. Pic: PA

item.title: Reynolds recruits former Balfour Beatty chief to nationalised British Steel
item.description: The former boss of Balfour Beatty, the infrastructure group, has been recruited by the government to join the board of the publicly owned British Steel.
item.media:description: Blast furnaces at British Steel's Scunthorpe plant. Pic: Reuters/ Dominic Lipinski

item.title: Football chiefs to hold crunch talks with regulator on £1.5bn New Deal
item.description: English football chiefs will hold crunch talks on Tuesday in a bid to thrash out a £1.5bn 10-year deal and avert the threat of a settlement imposed by the sport's new regulator.
item.media:description: Chelsea's Andrey Santos, left, scores his side's fifth goal during the English FA Cup quarterfinal soccer match between Chelsea and Port Vale in London, England, Saturday, April 4, 2026. (AP Photo/Ian Walton)

item.title: Heading on holiday soon? These travel money hints and tricks are must-read before you do
item.description: Britons spend billions of pounds abroad every year, but it can be difficult to know how to make your money go as far as possible.

item.title: J&J offers $5.5bn to settle baby powder lawsuits
item.description: Johnson & Johnson (J&J) has offered to pay $5.5bn (£4.13bn) to resolve tens of thousands of lawsuits in the US alleging its talcum powder caused ovarian cancer.
item.media:description: A bottle of Johnson and Johnson Baby Powder

item.title: Poultry farming leads to 100-fold increase in food-poisoning bacteria, study finds
item.description: Industrial poultry farming has led to a more than 100-fold increase in the spread of a bacteria causing food poisoning, scientists have discovered.
item.media:description: Chickens gather near water feeders at a poultry farm in Nashik, India, July 28, 2025. REUTERS/Francis Mascarenhas
